newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end slightly up after seesaw trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end slightly up after seesaw trade.

text.p: Philippine shares on Wednesday ended slightly higher after being locked in a tight range for most of the session as blue chip issues pared down losses, traders said.

"Some firstliner issues went back up towards close. But in general, the market remained mixed and sideways what with concerns about the peso opening at 29 to the dollar," said Carl Valentin, analyst at Asia Pacific Capital Equities.
The main index moved in a 13-point range during the session mostly staying in negative territory. It finally settled 2.96 points higher, or 0.11 percent, at 2,595.42.
Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co reversed its losses ending five pesos up at 930 pesos from an intra-day low of 915 pesos.
Magnum International Securities research head Mayenne Katimbang said despite pervading concerns about the currency, release of PLDT's first half earnings may cheer up the market.
PLDT said it will release its first half profits on Thursday.
Despite the market's uptick, decliners outnumbered gainers in the broad market 63 to 50 with 59 issues unchanged.
Turnover was smaller at 1.7 billion pesos from the previous day's 2.1 billion.

"A lot of money is parked in fixed income securities. People are looking for direction, for stability in the financial markets and for good first half earnings. Until then the market will remain sideways" said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities.
